Info: conditions, averages, classes

The questions are asked in Turkish, as original page images, unlike the Text tab, which uses English translations. A, text only, is the control, not a score; B and C are for setups that take images.

  • B · Picture alone. The crops of the page as the whole question, context first; instructions “Which option is correct?”; the options are the question's letters only. The crops are original Turkish pages, so B is a Turkish page-reading task.
  • A · Text only. The Turkish question text and options as the text test sends them, with the figure left out. Where a stem or an option exists only as a picture, the text holds a placeholder (“[Görsel seçenek X]”: 90 Logic and 6 Math texts; “[Görsel soru]” for one Math stem). A control: how much of each question the text alone answers, not a score.
  • C · Text + picture. Condition A's Turkish text, options and instructions, with the crops after the text.
  • D · OCR route. One OCR model's text of the crops (context first, joined by a blank line, layout tags removed) as the question, with B's instructions and letters. Each OCR model is a separate route; a setup's best route is shown.

Against the control, on all 358 questions (Logic and Math pooled):

  • B − A (picture alone against the control): +0.7 points · mean over 7 image models
  • C − A (text + picture against the control): +5.1 points · mean over 7 image models

Each line is the mean, over the models with both cells complete, of a model's accuracy in that condition minus its accuracy in A; one point is one percentage point.

Class: Size by total parameters, as disclosed by the maker (for MoE models the label also shows active parameters): Tiny under 6B · Small 6B–15B · Medium over 15B up to 40B · Large over 40B. Models of undisclosed size, by standard list price per 1M input tokens: Efficient up to $0.50 · Workhorse up to $3 · Flagship over $3. Undisclosed: neither a disclosed size nor a list price.

9,662 graded answers in 27 runs, read at build time.

Where the self-hosted models ran

  • d3-ultra · DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64, 121 GB unified memory) on spark2 · BF16 · server: d3_server.py (CPython 3.12.13; torch 2.14.1+cu130, transformers 5.17.0, accelerate 1.15.0, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2)
  • GLiDE 27B · DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64, 121 GB unified memory) on spark2 · BF16 · server: glide.server (fastino/GLiDE-27B@4d32743 (its glide package))
  • KnowLine-31B-Gen1.5 · DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64, 121 GB unified memory) on spark2 · BF16 · server: CPython 3.12.13; sglang 0.5.21, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1, flashinfer 0.6.18

API setups ran on their providers' services.

Method: questions, crops, conditions, OCR, runs and cost

Questions

  • 358 questions: Logic 306 (numerical reasoning 269, verbal reasoning 37); Math 52 (basic concepts 6, digits and place value 7, division and divisibility 33, prime factorisation and gcd/lcm 1, rational numbers 1, ordering 2, factorisation 2), from 5 books of the published question bank (not named here). They are the answered questions whose figure the text test could not carry: every Logic question with a figure crop, and the Math questions the text parser dropped for their images (each with a number and an answer-key entry; one has its options only as pictures).
  • One data issue: a Logic question printed its number inside its figure, so the text parser merged it into the shared context of the two questions after it. The vision track cuts that part out of both their crops and their text; that question itself is still missing from the benchmark.
  • All four conditions are in Turkish, with the original text and no translation; the Text tab's results come from English translations of the other questions.

Crops

  • 670 crops for 358 questions, on average 0.493 Mpx in 1.87 crops per question; 54 questions have 1 crop, 296 questions have 2 crops, 8 questions have 3 crops.
  • Boxes: the layout blocks of the book scans (MinerU content_list, a 0–1000 grid of the page). Pages rendered with PyMuPDF at zoom 2.5; 6 px padding (the blocks are tight on the glyphs). Crops under 280 px high are padded with white below (136), crops over 1568 px a side scaled down (0).
  • Context first, then the question; one crop per page column, so a question that runs on into the next column or page gets one crop per column.
  • Answer keys are separate lines or strips on the page; no block of a key line lies inside any crop (0 found).
  • Each question's blocks were found again on the page from its figure, its own number and its shared context, growing over neighbouring blocks of its text and stopping at another question's number, a group header or an answer key; questions with weak text coverage were listed and looked at. Every box was checked to sit on its text in all five books.
  • Checked by eye: 30 questions from the five books (six at random per book plus every question the locator flagged). The review led to three fixes (the merged question above; a question's own figure cut as a “context” crop; options printed side by side split by the first column rule). After them every reviewed crop holds the whole question and nothing of its neighbours; the only foreign block is a book ornament inside one context box.

Conditions

  • A · Control: text without the figure. The Turkish question text and options as the text test sends them, with the figure left out. Where a stem or an option exists only as a picture, the text holds a placeholder (“[Görsel seçenek X]”: 90 Logic and 6 Math texts; “[Görsel soru]” for one Math stem). A control: how much of each question the text alone answers, not a score.
  • B · Crop only. The crops of the page as the whole question, context first; instructions “Which option is correct?”; the options are the question's letters only. The crops are original Turkish pages, so B is a Turkish page-reading task.
  • C · Text + crop. Condition A's Turkish text, options and instructions, with the crops after the text.
  • D · OCR of the crop. One OCR model's text of the crops (context first, joined by a blank line, layout tags removed) as the question, with B's instructions and letters. Each OCR model is a separate route; a setup's best route is shown.

The method follows the Turkish decision-model benchmark's page-image track. One question per request; the request is built by the benchmark runner's own code, with the images in each provider's format.

OCR (condition D)

No OCR model has read the crops yet, so condition D has no results. Planned, as in the Turkish decision-model benchmark's page-image track: Chandra OCR 2, dots.mocr, Surya OCR 2 and Baidu Unlimited-OCR-2, each its own D route, with each OCR model's character error rate measured against the clean text where it exists (normalised Levenshtein, micro-averaged over crops, the median also given).

Measures

  • Accuracy over the questions of the part; a refusal or a letter outside the options counts as wrong. Its 95% Wilson interval shows on hover or tap.
  • Tie group: setups in accuracy order, every pair compared on the same questions with the exact McNemar test, Holm's correction over the pairs; two setups share a letter unless the corrected p < 0.05 (as on the Text tab).
  • Points: a model's accuracy in a condition minus its accuracy in A, in percentage points; the averages under the results (behind '*') are over the models that have both cells on all 358 questions.
  • Logic and Math are reported separately and pooled. The vision results are ranked apart from the Text tab.

Runs

Decision setups ran each condition once on both benchmarks: a 20-question smoke run per benchmark, the runner's probability check, then the full run (306 Logic, 52 Math). Chat setups (setup lm-chat-vision-1, condition B only) ran once per benchmark with no smoke gate and no probabilities: one question per request, the letter of the reply's last “CEVAP: X” line scored, and a reply cut off or without that line counted wrong; their measure is accuracy only. Only complete cells are scored; every other setup of the track is listed with its state and the answers stored so far.
